title: The Comprehensive List of AI Red Teaming Tools

tools.name: DeepTeam
tools.description: DeepTeam is an open-source LLM red-teaming framework covering 120+ vulnerability types and 20+ single- and multi-turn attack methods, with mappings to OWASP, NIST AI RMF, and MITRE ATLAS. Docs

tools.name: PyRIT
tools.description: PyRIT is Microsoft's Python Risk Identification Toolkit for generative AI, used by Microsoft's AI Red Team to automate adversarial probing with configurable targets, converters, scorers, and multi-turn orchestrators.

tools.name: Confident AI
tools.description: Confident AI is an AI quality platform for enterprise teams to standardize evals and observability, with native red teaming and AI governance gates that block releases failing vulnerability checks.

tools.name: promptfoo red teaming
tools.description: promptfoo's MIT-licensed red-teaming module scans applications for injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, and authorization flaws. OpenAI announced an agreement to acquire Promptfoo in March 2026. GitHub · Announcement

tools.name: garak
tools.description: garak, from NVIDIA, is a generative-AI red-teaming and vulnerability framework whose plugin architecture composes probes, generators, buffs, and detectors into automated attack runs. Paper

tools.name: Giskard
tools.description: Giskard is an open-source testing library for LLM agents and ML models whose scan automatically detects vulnerabilities including prompt injection, harmful content, hallucination, and sycophancy.

tools.name: Moonshot
tools.description: Moonshot, from the AI Verify Foundation, is a modular toolkit that combines benchmarking and red teaming of LLM applications behind a single API, CLI, and web UI.

tools.name: Rogue
tools.description: Rogue is a source-available AI-agent evaluation and red-teaming platform from Qualifire (Rogue Security); its proprietary license permits personal and internal use but requires separate licensing for commercial hosting.

tools.name: Inspect AI
tools.description: Inspect AI, from the UK AI Security Institute, is an evaluation framework whose solvers, scorers, and sandboxed tool use support safety and adversarial evaluations, including agentic attack scenarios. Docs

tools.name: Agentic Security
tools.description: Agentic Security is an open-source LLM vulnerability scanner and red-teaming CLI that fuzzes endpoints with jailbreak datasets, multi-step attacks, and stress tests.

tools.name: FuzzyAI
tools.description: FuzzyAI, from CyberArk, fuzzes LLM APIs with strategies including adversarial suffixes, genetic search, and encoding to identify jailbreaks and guardrail bypasses.

tools.name: Prompt Fuzzer
tools.description: Prompt Fuzzer, from Prompt Security (now a SentinelOne company), tests system prompts with prompt-injection and jailbreak attacks and scores the resulting resilience.

tools.name: promptmap
tools.description: promptmap is a prompt-injection scanner that tests a custom LLM application's system prompt with rule-based attack cases and reports which ones leak or override it.

tools.name: spikee
tools.description: spikee, from Reversec Labs, is a modular toolkit for testing LLMs, guardrails, and applications against prompt injection and jailbreak attacks and for generating targeted test datasets.

tools.name: llm-attacks (GCG)
tools.description: llm-attacks is the reference implementation of Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), which optimizes universal, transferable adversarial suffixes that jailbreak aligned models. Paper

tools.name: PAIR
tools.description: PAIR (Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement) uses attacker, target, and judge models to iteratively refine jailbreak prompts in black-box settings. Paper

tools.name: TAP
tools.description: TAP (Tree of Attacks with Pruning) extends PAIR with tree-of-thought search and pruning to jailbreak black-box models query-efficiently. Paper

tools.name: AutoDAN
tools.description: AutoDAN generates stealthy, human-readable jailbreak prompts via a hierarchical genetic algorithm, evading perplexity-based filters that catch gradient suffixes. Paper

tools.name: GPTFuzz
tools.description: GPTFuzz is a black-box jailbreak fuzzer that mutates human-written seed templates and uses a judge model to grow an attack corpus automatically. Paper

tools.name: EasyJailbreak
tools.description: EasyJailbreak provides a common interface for implementing, constructing, and evaluating multiple jailbreak methods. Paper

tools.name: DeepInception
tools.description: DeepInception is a prompt-only jailbreak that nests a model inside layered fictional scenarios to erode its safety guardrails. Paper

tools.name: PromptInject
tools.description: PromptInject is the framework accompanying the "Ignore Previous Prompt" paper, quantifying goal hijacking and prompt leaking via mask-based iterative adversarial prompt composition. Paper

tools.name: ArtPrompt
tools.description: ArtPrompt is an ASCII-art-based jailbreak that hides unsafe words in text art to bypass token-level safety filters. Paper

tools.name: Open-Prompt-Injection
tools.description: Open-Prompt-Injection is a research framework implementing standardized prompt-injection attacks and defenses for reproducible evaluation. Paper

tools.name: BIPIA
tools.description: BIPIA, from Microsoft, benchmarks indirect prompt injection across email QA, web QA, table QA, summarization, and code QA, with black-box and white-box defense baselines. Paper

tools.name: HouYi
tools.description: HouYi is a black-box prompt-injection attack framework that systematically composes a framework, separator, and disruptor to hijack LLM-integrated applications. Paper

tools.name: Tensor Trust
tools.description: Tensor Trust is a prompt-injection attack-and-defense game from UC Berkeley whose gameplay produced a public dataset of human-crafted injections and defenses. Paper

tools.name: deepset prompt-injections
tools.description: The deepset prompt-injections dataset is an Apache-2.0 labeled corpus of injection and benign prompts for training and evaluating injection classifiers.

tools.name: Lakera PINT Benchmark
tools.description: PINT (Prompt Injection Test), from Lakera, provides a dataset and harness for evaluating prompt-injection detectors without training on the test set.

tools.name: Adversarial Robustness Toolbox
tools.description: ART, from the Linux Foundation AI & Data (originally IBM), provides evasion, poisoning, extraction, and inference attacks and defenses for multiple machine-learning frameworks and data modalities.

tools.name: Foolbox
tools.description: Foolbox creates adversarial examples against PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX models using gradient-based, decision-based, and score-based attacks.

tools.name: CleverHans
tools.description: CleverHans provides reference adversarial-example attack implementations for benchmarking model robustness.

tools.name: TextAttack
tools.description: TextAttack is a framework for adversarial attacks, data augmentation, and adversarial training in NLP, with many recipe-based text attacks.

tools.name: OpenAttack
tools.description: OpenAttack, from THUNLP, is a textual adversarial attack toolkit supporting sentence-, word-, and character-level attacks and attack evaluation.

tools.name: AdvBox
tools.description: AdvBox, from Baidu, is a toolbox for generating adversarial examples and testing the robustness of models across multiple deep-learning frameworks.

tools.name: Armory
tools.description: Armory, from Two Six Technologies, is an adversarial-ML evaluation testbed built for the DARPA GARD program, orchestrating scenario-based robustness experiments.

tools.name: Check Point AI Red Teaming
tools.description: Check Point AI Red Teaming, built from the Lakera acquisition, runs adversarial assessments against models and agents and draws attack intelligence from the Gandalf community.

tools.name: Mindgard
tools.description: Mindgard is an automated AI red-teaming and offensive-security platform that maps attack surfaces and continuously tests models, agents, applications, and infrastructure.

tools.name: HiddenLayer
tools.description: HiddenLayer provides automated red teaming and attack simulation for generative, agentic, and predictive AI, alongside model scanning and runtime detection and response.

tools.name: Agent Torture Lab
tools.description: Agent Torture Lab is a commercial AI-agent testing service that probes customer-support bots for policy, privacy, and escalation failures and returns evidence-linked transcripts with a fix plan and retest plan.

tools.name: Cisco AI Defense
tools.description: Cisco AI Defense, built on the Robust Intelligence acquisition, provides algorithmic red teaming and runtime guardrails for enterprise AI applications.

tools.name: Haize Labs
tools.description: Haize Labs builds domain-specific agents with a proprietary Reliability Harness that combines simulation testing, adversarial red teaming, guardrails, and evaluation judges.

tools.name: Prisma AIRS AI Red Teaming
tools.description: Prisma AIRS AI Red Teaming, incorporating technology from Palo Alto Networks' Protect AI acquisition, runs adaptive adversarial assessments against AI applications and agents.

tools.name: Adversa AI
tools.description: Adversa AI provides continuous red teaming, threat modeling, and remediation for custom AI agents, applications, models, APIs, and MCP-connected infrastructure.

tools.name: F5 AI Red Team
tools.description: F5 AI Red Team, built from the CalypsoAI acquisition, uses adversarial agents to test models and applications for prompt injection, jailbreaks, and other AI-specific vulnerabilities.

tools.name: Zscaler Automated AI Red Teaming
tools.description: Zscaler Automated AI Red Teaming, built from the SPLX acquisition, continuously tests GenAI applications with customizable probes and integrates findings into development and governance workflows.

tools.name: Enkrypt AI
tools.description: Enkrypt AI offers automated red teaming, risk assessment, and guardrails for LLM applications, with compliance-oriented reporting.

tools.name: Gray Swan Shade
tools.description: Shade runs adaptive adversarial campaigns against models, agents, guardrails, and deployment contexts using attack intelligence from Gray Swan's Arena research environment.

tools.name: Repello AI ARTEMIS
tools.description: ARTEMIS is Repello AI's automated red-teaming engine for continuous adversarial testing of LLM applications, RAG pipelines, and agentic systems, with CI/CD integration.

tools.name: Patronus AI
tools.description: Patronus AI's evaluation platform supports OWASP-aligned adversarial datasets, custom attack generation, evaluators, and simulated environments for testing AI models and agents.

tools.name: NeMo Guardrails
tools.description: NeMo Guardrails is NVIDIA's toolkit for programmable guardrails (via Colang) on conversational systems, with topic control, jailbreak detection, and fact-checking rails.

tools.name: Guardrails AI
tools.description: Guardrails AI is a Python framework for input/output validation, with a community Guardrails Hub of validators for injection, PII, and toxicity.

tools.name: LlamaFirewall
tools.description: LlamaFirewall, from Meta, is an open-source guardrail framework for agentic systems that combines PromptGuard, agent-alignment checks, and code-safety scanning.

tools.name: Invariant Guardrails
tools.description: Invariant Guardrails is an Apache-2.0 rule-based layer for agentic systems that enforces policies over messages and tool calls; Snyk acquired Invariant Labs in 2025.

tools.name: Llama Guard
tools.description: Llama Guard is Meta's family of downloadable safety-classifier models for input and output moderation, released under Meta's community license as part of Purple Llama.

tools.name: Prompt Guard
tools.description: Prompt Guard, from Meta, is an 86M-parameter downloadable classifier that flags prompt-injection and jailbreak strings in user inputs and retrieved content.

tools.name: ShieldGemma
tools.description: ShieldGemma, from Google, is a family of Gemma-based safety-classifier models for filtering harmful content in prompts and responses.

tools.name: Granite Guardian
tools.description: Granite Guardian, from IBM, is an Apache-2.0 family of downloadable guardrail models for detecting harm, jailbreaks, and RAG groundedness and relevance risks.

tools.name: Check Point AI Agent Security
tools.description: Check Point AI Agent Security, formerly Lakera Guard, enforces runtime policies across prompts, responses, external content, and agent tool calls.

tools.name: Azure AI Content Safety
tools.description: Azure AI Content Safety provides content moderation plus Prompt Shields for direct and indirect prompt attacks, groundedness detection, and agent task-adherence checks.

tools.name: Google Model Armor
tools.description: Model Armor is Google Cloud's service for screening LLM prompts and responses for injection, jailbreaks, sensitive data, malicious URLs, and harmful content.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
tools.description: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applies configurable safety policies — content filters, denied topics, and contextual grounding checks — to Bedrock applications.

tools.name: OpenAI Moderation
tools.description: The OpenAI Moderation endpoint is a free hosted API for text and image safety classification.

tools.name: AgentDojo
tools.description: AgentDojo, from ETH Zurich, is a dynamic environment for evaluating prompt-injection attacks and defenses against tool-using LLM agents on realistic tasks. Paper

tools.name: InjecAgent
tools.description: InjecAgent is a benchmark for indirect prompt-injection attacks against tool-integrated agents, measuring both direct harm and data-exfiltration outcomes. Paper

tools.name: Agent Security Bench
tools.description: Agent Security Bench (ASB) formalizes and benchmarks a broad range of attacks and defenses on LLM agents, including direct/indirect injection, memory poisoning, and backdoors. Paper

tools.name: ToolEmu
tools.description: ToolEmu uses an LLM to emulate tool execution so agents can be stress-tested for risky behavior in high-stakes scenarios without real side effects. Paper

tools.name: Agentic Radar
tools.description: Agentic Radar, created by SPLX before its Zscaler acquisition, maps an agentic workflow's tools and dependencies and probes it for security weaknesses.

tools.name: AgentHarm
tools.description: AgentHarm, from the UK AI Security Institute and Gray Swan AI, measures harmful multi-step agent behavior and jailbreak transfer; its license restricts use to improving AI safety and security. Paper

tools.name: JailbreakBench
tools.description: JailbreakBench is an open robustness benchmark for jailbreaking, with a standardized dataset, evaluation pipeline, leaderboard, and artifact repository. Paper

tools.name: HarmBench
tools.description: HarmBench provides a standardized set of harmful behaviors and a validation classifier for comparing attack success and refusal robustness across methods. Paper

tools.name: StrongREJECT
tools.description: StrongREJECT pairs forbidden prompts with an autograder that scores refusal, specificity, and convincingness to measure whether a jailbreak produces actionable harmful content. Paper

tools.name: JailbreakV-28K
tools.description: JailbreakV-28K contains 20,000 text-based transfer attacks and 8,000 image-based attacks for testing jailbreak robustness in multimodal large language models. Paper

tools.name: SORRY-Bench
tools.description: SORRY-Bench evaluates refusal behavior with 440 balanced instructions across 44 unsafe topics and 20 linguistic augmentations. Paper

tools.name: h4rm3l
tools.description: h4rm3l is a domain-specific language and benchmark for composing novel jailbreak attacks programmatically and measuring their success. Paper

tools.name: AILuminate
tools.description: AILuminate is MLCommons' safety-benchmark family covering 12 hazard categories. Its Apache-2.0 repository provides an offline demo; practice and official tests use separately licensed or confidential prompt sets. Website

tools.name: DecodingTrust
tools.description: DecodingTrust assesses toxicity, stereotype bias, adversarial robustness, out-of-distribution robustness, privacy, machine ethics, and fairness (NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper). Paper

tools.name: TrustLLM
tools.description: TrustLLM benchmarks trustworthiness across truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, and machine ethics. Paper

tools.name: SafetyBench
tools.description: SafetyBench is a multiple-choice LLM safety evaluation across seven harm categories in English and Chinese. Paper

tools.name: Do-Not-Answer
tools.description: Do-Not-Answer is a dataset of questions responsible models should refuse, with an evaluation protocol for safeguard effectiveness. Paper

tools.name: XSTest
tools.description: XSTest tests exaggerated safety (over-refusal) using safe prompts that superficially resemble unsafe ones. Paper

tools.name: ToxiGen
tools.description: ToxiGen is a publicly downloadable dataset of synthetic implicit toxic and benign statements mentioning 13 minority groups; its dataset card specifies no license, and Microsoft has archived the original code repository. Code · Paper

tools.name: WMDP
tools.description: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy) measures hazardous knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemistry as a proxy for dangerous capabilities. Paper

tools.name: CyberSecEval
tools.description: CyberSecEval, part of Meta's Purple Llama project, benchmarks cybersecurity risks and capabilities including insecure code generation, prompt injection, cyberattack helpfulness, and defensive tasks.

tools.name: SALAD-Bench
tools.description: SALAD-Bench is a hierarchical safety benchmark for LLMs, attacks, and defenses, paired with an MD-Judge evaluator across a structured harm taxonomy. Paper

tools.name: BeaverTails
tools.description: BeaverTails, from PKU-Alignment, is a QA dataset with separate helpfulness and harmlessness annotations for safety alignment research. Paper

tools.name: In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts
tools.description: In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts collects 15,000+ jailbreak prompts, including DAN-family prompts, from public platforms for studying attacks observed in practice. Paper

tools.name: AdvBench
tools.description: AdvBench is the harmful-behaviors and harmful-strings dataset introduced with GCG as a target set for jailbreak research. Paper

tools.name: HackAPrompt Dataset
tools.description: HackAPrompt contains 600,000+ adversarial prompts submitted to a global prompt-hacking competition; the MIT-licensed dataset requires accepting Hugging Face access conditions. Paper

tools.name: HarmfulQA
tools.description: HarmfulQA, from DeCLaRe Lab, is an Apache-2.0 dataset of harmful questions and red-teaming conversations created with the Chain of Utterances method. Paper

tools.name: ToxicChat
tools.description: ToxicChat, from LMSYS, contains toxicity and jailbreak labels for real user queries to a chatbot; prompts and outputs are licensed CC-BY-NC-4.0. Paper

tools.name: MM-SafetyBench
tools.description: MM-SafetyBench evaluates multimodal-LLM safety against query-relevant image-based jailbreaks; its dataset is restricted to noncommercial research under CC-BY-NC-4.0. Paper

tools.name: ForbiddenQuestions
tools.description: ForbiddenQuestions pairs policy-violating questions with jailbreak prompts to measure attack success across scenarios. Paper

tools.name: ModelScan
tools.category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
tools.description: ModelScan scans model files, including pickle, HDF5, and SavedModel formats, for code that executes on load and other model-serialization threats.

tools.name: picklescan
tools.category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
tools.description: picklescan analyzes Python pickle files for suspicious imports and opcodes, and is integrated into Hugging Face Hub's malware scanning.

tools.name: Fickling
tools.category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
tools.description: Fickling, from Trail of Bits, is a decompiler, static analyzer, and bytecode rewriter for pickle files, used to detect and craft malicious payloads for testing.

tools.name: safetensors
tools.category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
tools.description: safetensors is a safe serialization format for model weights that avoids the arbitrary-code-execution behavior of pickle-based checkpoints.

tools.name: HiddenLayer Model Scanner
tools.category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
tools.description: HiddenLayer's Model Scanner statically inspects model artifacts for malware, backdoors, and integrity issues before they enter production.

tools.name: Prisma AIRS AI Model Security
tools.category: Model and ML Supply-Chain Security Scanning
tools.description: Prisma AIRS AI Model Security, incorporating Protect AI technology, scans model architecture, weights, operators, dependencies, and embedded code before deployment.

tools.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
tools.description: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications is a community-maintained risk list covering prompt injection, sensitive-information disclosure, supply-chain weaknesses, and other GenAI application risks.

tools.name: MITRE ATLAS
tools.description: MITRE ATLAS is an ATT&CK-style knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques against AI systems, backed by real-world case studies.

tools.name: OWASP ML Security Top 10
tools.description: The OWASP Machine Learning Security Top 10 catalogs risks to classic ML systems, such as data poisoning and model inversion.

tools.name: AI Vulnerability Database
tools.description: AVID is a public database and taxonomy of AI failure modes and vulnerabilities, providing a common reporting schema for the community.

tools.name: AI Incident Database
tools.description: The AI Incident Database, from the Responsible AI Collaborative, indexes reported real-world AI harms and near-misses to inform threat modeling.

tools.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
tools.description: The NIST AI RMF is a voluntary U.S. framework for governing AI risk, with a Generative AI profile addressing risks specific to generative systems.

tools.name: Google Secure AI Framework (SAIF)
tools.description: SAIF is Google's published conceptual framework and risk map for securing AI systems across the development and deployment lifecycle.

tools.name: Counterfit
tools.description: Counterfit remains public and unarchived, but its latest release dates to November 2022 and its latest functional code changes to April 2023; PyRIT is Microsoft's current generative-AI red-teaming framework.

tools.name: LLMFuzzer
tools.description: LLMFuzzer's maintainers explicitly mark the project as unmaintained and invite users to fork it.

tools.name: Vigil
tools.description: Vigil is not formally archived, but its latest release was in December 2023, its latest code update was in January 2024, and its README describes it as alpha research software.

tools.name: Rebuff
tools.description: Protect AI archived Rebuff in May 2025; the repository remains available under Apache-2.0.

tools.name: LLM Guard
tools.description: Protect AI archived LLM Guard in July 2026 and states that the project and associated models are no longer developed or maintained.

tools.name: Robust Intelligence
tools.description: Cisco acquired Robust Intelligence in October 2024; its algorithmic red teaming is now part of Cisco AI Defense.

tools.name: Prompt Security
tools.description: SentinelOne completed its acquisition of Prompt Security in 2025; Prompt Security now operates within the SentinelOne Singularity platform.

tools.name: Protect AI
tools.description: Palo Alto Networks acquired Protect AI in July 2025 and integrated its model scanning, red teaming, and runtime technology into Prisma AIRS.

tools.name: CalypsoAI
tools.description: F5 announced its agreement to acquire CalypsoAI in September 2025; F5 now describes F5 AI Red Team and F5 AI Guardrails as generally available products stemming from the acquisition.

secondary_links.label: F5 AI Red Team and F5 AI Guardrails

tools.name: SPLX
tools.description: Zscaler acquired SPLX in November 2025 and integrated its discovery, automated red teaming, and governance technology into Zscaler AI Security.

tools.name: Lakera
tools.description: Check Point completed its acquisition of Lakera in October 2025; Lakera Red and Lakera Guard were succeeded by Check Point AI Red Teaming and AI Agent Security.

tools.name: Invariant Labs
tools.description: Snyk acquired Invariant Labs in June 2025; the Apache-2.0 Invariant Guardrails repository remains public while its technology contributes to Snyk's AI security products and research.
